test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 17 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Two taps can fill a cistern in 3 hours and 57 hours, respectively. A third tap can empty it in 3 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill one-third of the empty cistern, if all of them are opened together?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net efficiency = Tap A + Tap B − Tap C

Tap A (3 hr) and Tap C (3 hr) cancel each other out (fill = empty).

Only Tap B (57 hr) contributes to filling the cistern.

Time to fill 1/3 cistern = (Total time for B) ÷ 3 = 57 ÷ 3 = 19 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 19 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling time Tap A = 3 hr, Tap B = 57 hr. Emptying time Tap C = 3 hr.

**Formula Used:** Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

⇒ Total Efficiency = 19 + 1 − 19 = 1

⇒ Total Work = 57 units

⇒ Required Work = 1/3 × 57 = 19 units

⇒ Time required = Required Work ÷ Total Efficiency

⇒ Time = 19 ÷ 1 = 19 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 19 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Efficiency

Filling pipes have **positive efficiency**, while emptying pipes (leakages) have **negative efficiency** in calculations.

Total Work Concept

The capacity of the cistern is usually taken as the **LCM** of the individual times taken by the pipes to fill/empty it.

Combined Time Formula

For two pipes filling in 'a' and 'b' hours and one emptying in 'c' hours, the combined rate is (1/a + 1/b − 1/c).</p
